<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="6" type="chapter">
               <ns0:head>CHAP. VI.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p n="1">1. TAke heed that you do not your alms be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore men to be seen of them, otherwise ye have no reward <ns0:note n="‖" place="margin">Or, <ns0:hi>
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ith.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> of your Father which is in heaven.<ns0:note place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Alms</ns0:hi> are any Acts of kindness freely done by us, for the relief of any that are <ns0:hi>in Destress</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Misery,</ns0:hi> which when they are done, from a Principle of <ns0:hi>love to</ns0:hi> God, his Precepts, commanding them Obedience in Faith to his Promises made to the giving of them, and that he may be Glorified, are truly <ns0:hi>good Works,</ns0:hi> Acts of Religion, and Acceptable to God, tho Meritorious of nothing from him. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 10.31. otherwise they are meerly Acts of <ns0:hi>Humanity</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Morality</ns0:hi> to the reward of which God is by no promise Obliged. Therefore Christs Disciples are Obliged, to take heed that in the doing of their <ns0:hi>Alms,</ns0:hi> tho they may do them before Men, that God may be Glorifyed, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 2.15. 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 2.12. yet they do them not be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fore Men, on purpose that they should take notice of them, and Applaud them for them, for God rewardeth no Action, of which he is not the <ns0:hi>End.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2. Therefore when thou dost <ns0:hi>thine</ns0:hi> alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crites <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">
                     <ns0:hi>Or ca<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>se <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> a Trump<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                           <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> 
                        <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 word">
                           <ns0:desc>〈◊〉</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> be soun<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ed<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> do in the synagogues, and in the streets<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> that they may have glory of men. Verily, I say unto you, They have their reward.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doth.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 That thy <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Lu. 14.1<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 14.</ns0:note> alms may be in secret, and thy Father which seeth in secret, himself shall reward thee openly.<ns0:note place="bottom">There are some who think that our Saviour here reflects upon some Practice of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees</ns0:hi> then in use, for <ns0:hi>Osten<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tation,</ns0:hi> who under a pretence of a mean to call People toge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, caused a <ns0:hi>Trumpet</ns0:hi> to be sounded, when they distributed their Alms, but those learned in their Writings assure us, they could never find in them any Foundation for such an Opinion. The Speech is rather <ns0:hi>Metaphorical,</ns0:hi> Prohibiting all <ns0:hi>Ostentation</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Acts of Charity,</ns0:hi> and inviting other to take no<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tice of them, as <ns0:hi>Iehu</ns0:hi> invited <ns0:hi>Ionadab</ns0:hi> to come and see his <ns0:hi>Zeal,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 10, 16. As the 3<ns0:hi>d. v.</ns0:hi> is but a Proverbial Ex<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pression expounded <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 4. <ns0:hi>That thy Alms may be in Secret.</ns0:hi> Not that it is not lawful to give a poor Body Money, or Bread, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> in the sight of others: but only to do it for that End, that <ns0:hi>we might be seen of others,</ns0:hi> the thing forbidden un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der the <ns0:hi>Metaphorical</ns0:hi> Expression is <ns0:hi>Ostentation,</ns0:hi> and seeking our own <ns0:hi>Honour,</ns0:hi> and applause. The thing commanded is <ns0:hi>Sincerity</ns0:hi> with Respect to our <ns0:hi>End.</ns0:hi> The Apos<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>le calls it a <ns0:hi>giving with Simplicity,</ns0:hi> singly aiming at the Glorifying of God, by an Obedient performance of our Duty: He tells us those who give their Alms to be honoured of Men, <ns0:hi>have their reward,</ns0:hi> that is, all which they are like to have, Men applaud and cry them up, there's their reward: Others <ns0:hi>shall have their reward from God, who seeth in secret,</ns0:hi> and so needeth not such a Publication of our good Deeds, and he will reward them openly before Men, and <ns0:hi>Angels</ns0:hi> at the last day, <ns0:hi>Chap<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                     </ns0:hi> 25.34, 36, 37. and ordinarily in this Life, <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 113.9, 10. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 37.25. <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 41.1.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:227" />5 And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites <ns0:hi>are,</ns0:hi> for they love to pray, standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men, Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour here cautioneth them against the same thing in <ns0:hi>Prayer,</ns0:hi> as he had done before in <ns0:hi>giving Alms,</ns0:hi> viz. <ns0:hi>Hypocri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sie</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ostentation,</ns0:hi> doing this Duty upon that Design meerly to be taken notice of, and applauded by Men, it was Lawful to pray <ns0:hi>standing in the Synagogues,</ns0:hi> but not to do it <ns0:hi>meerly</ns0:hi> to be taken notice of by Men, for devout Persons, nor yet to confine themselves to praying in the <ns0:hi>Synagogues,</ns0:hi> if they chose to pray <ns0:hi>standing,</ns0:hi> that they might be more Conspicuous, and in the <ns0:hi>Synagogues</ns0:hi>; because those places were more Holy (as they might Dream) Or, which seems rather to be here meant, be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause there most People would see them, for which purpose only, they chose <ns0:hi>Corners of Streets,</ns0:hi> as was the old <ns0:hi>Popish Custom,</ns0:hi> upon which Account they set up <ns0:hi>Crosses,</ns0:hi> at three way Leets, &c. these things were sinful, but to pray <ns0:hi>standing</ns0:hi> was usual, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 11.25. and to pray in the <ns0:hi>Synagogues,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>in the Temple standing</ns0:hi> as usual, <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 18.13. But those who do it meerly for <ns0:hi>Vain-Glory, have their reward,</ns0:hi> and must expect none from God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 But thou, when thou prayest <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">2 Kin. 4.33.</ns0:note> enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut to thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret, and thy Father which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.<ns0:note place="bottom">By this, <ns0:hi>Publick Prayer</ns0:hi> is not Condemned, but <ns0:hi>secret Prayer</ns0:hi> is Established, and made every Christians Duty, and Christi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ans are warned not to think that their <ns0:hi>Duty of Prayer</ns0:hi> is dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />charged by their going to <ns0:hi>places of Publick Worship</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Praying</ns0:hi> there, but that which our Saviour here cautioneth us against, is <ns0:hi>Ostentation,</ns0:hi> by which Men may as much offend in their Closets as elsewhere, wherever we pray, we must take heed that our Ends be right, that the Glory of God be our Principal end, and yielding Obedience to his Command, and there is no better means in Order to this, than the right setting of God before our Eyes, as he that <ns0:hi>seeth in secret,</ns0:hi> and knoweth the most secret Designs, Scopes, and Intentions of our Hearts, and who if we thus perform our Duty, will reward us of his <ns0:hi>Free Grace and Mercy</ns0:hi>; not as Persons, who by our Prayers have merited any thing at his hand (for what <ns0:hi>Merit</ns0:hi> can there be in our Prayers, but as having shewed our Obedience to his Will, and in the fulfilling of those many Promises which he hath made to those that seek his Face, for the hearing of their Prayers.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 But when ye pray use not vain repetiti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, as the heathens do, for they think they shall be heard for their much speaking.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 Be not ye therefore like unto them, for your Father knows what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.<ns0:note place="bottom">It appeareth from hence, and from what followeth also, that the <ns0:hi>Praying</ns0:hi> here spoken of, is <ns0:hi>Vocal Prayer,</ns0:hi> not the meer Homage which the Heart payeth to God, by a Recognition of him as the Fountain of all Good, and our secret Desires that God would supply our Wants, but the <ns0:hi>Expression of those Desires</ns0:hi> by the <ns0:hi>words of our Mouths,</ns0:hi> which is that Duty which the Scripture generally calleth <ns0:hi>Prayer,</ns0:hi> and is most certainly a Duty incumbent on every Person. Nor are <ns0:hi>Repetitions</ns0:hi> of the same Requests in Prayer, or <ns0:hi>much speak<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing</ns0:hi> (that is <ns0:hi>Praying to some length of time</ns0:hi>) here absolutly forbidden: Our Saviour before his Passion prayed thrice, for the same thing within a short Compass of time (tho he did not use the same words) and <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 6.12. <ns0:hi>he continued all Night in Prayer to God.</ns0:hi> But that which is here forbidden, is an <ns0:hi>Opinion</ns0:hi> of being <ns0:hi>heard, for over long Prayers,</ns0:hi> and using <ns0:hi>Vain Repetitions</ns0:hi> as the <ns0:hi>Priests</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Baal,</ns0:hi> continued from Morning to Night crying, O <ns0:hi>Baal hear us</ns0:hi>! O <ns0:hi>Baal hear us,</ns0:hi> (as if their God had been asleep, or gone a Journey, as the Prophet mocketh them, 1 <ns0:hi>Kin.</ns0:hi> 18.27, 28) <ns0:hi>Repetitions</ns0:hi> are then <ns0:hi>Vain,</ns0:hi> when they are <ns0:hi>affected</ns0:hi> and flow from some irre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />verent Thoughts we have of God: Not when they are as it were forced from the <ns0:hi>Heat</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Intension of our Affections.</ns0:hi> The like is to be <ns0:hi>said</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>much speaking in Prayer.</ns0:hi> Long Prayers are not to be Condemned, but the <ns0:hi>Affectation</ns0:hi> of them is, and <ns0:hi>Long Prayers</ns0:hi> upon Pretences, and Designs are: But when the mind is <ns0:hi>attent,</ns0:hi> and the <ns0:hi>Affections servent,</ns0:hi> length of Prayer is no Fault, especially upon solemn Occasi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons, when we come not to ask a particular Mercy at the hand of God, nor for a particular Person, or Family. But Repetitions after the manner of Heathens, are Condemned as proceeding from irreverent Thoughts of God, as if he did not know what things we have need of, or were like a Man to be prevail'd upon by a multitude of Words.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 After this manner therefore pray ye, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 11.2.</ns0:note> Our Father which art in Heaven, Hallowed be thy name.<ns0:note place="bottom">Not always in <ns0:hi>these words,</ns0:hi> but always to this Sense, and in this manner. None ever thought <ns0:hi>Christians</ns0:hi> obliged to use no other words than these in Prayer, tho none must deny the Lawfulness of using those words which Christ hath sanctified <ns0:hi>After this manner</ns0:hi>: First seeking the Kingdom of God, and begging those things which more immediately concern God's Glory, and then those things which more immediately con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cern your selves. Or, <ns0:hi>After this manner,</ns0:hi> praying only in <ns0:hi>particular</ns0:hi> for such things, as are more generally couched in the following Petitions. <ns0:hi>Our Father which art in Heaven</ns0:hi>: A Compellation speaking our Faith, both in the <ns0:hi>Power,</ns0:hi> and in the <ns0:hi>Goodness</ns0:hi> of God, our eying him as in Heaven, speaketh his Power, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 115.3. our considering him as <ns0:hi>our Father,</ns0:hi> speaks our Faith in his Goodness, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 7.11. <ns0:hi>Hallowed be thy Name.</ns0:hi> Gods Name is whatsoever he hath made himself known by, let the Lord be Glorified in every thing, whereby he hath made himself known.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="10">10 Thy Kingdom come, Thy will be done in earth, as <ns0:hi>it is</ns0:hi> in heaven<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
                  <ns0:note place="bottom">Let the Lord rule over all the Nations of the Earth, and let them be freely subject to his Laws, and to his Son Jesus Christ, let the <ns0:hi>Gospel of the Kingdom</ns0:hi> be published, and prosper by bringing all Thoughts into a Captivity to it<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> And let the Kingdom of God come more within the Hearts of all Men, and hasten the <ns0:hi>Revelations</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Kingdom of Glory.</ns0:hi> Let the Will of the Lord be every where done, and that on Earth, with as much Freedom, and Cheerfulness, and with as little Reluctancy as it is done by the <ns0:hi>Angels</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Saints in Heaven.</ns0:hi> These three first Petitions are of great Cognation one to ano<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther, God is then Glorified when his Kingdom is advanced, and his Kingdom is then promoved, when there is most free and cheerful Obedience yielded to his Will, the sum is: <ns0:hi>Let God be Glorified.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="11">11 Give us this day, our daily bread.<ns0:note place="bottom">And for as much as in thee, we live, and move, and have our Life, so the means for the upholding, and the preserving of our Lives, and the Blessing upon them must be from thee, we beseech thee to give us Food convenient for us, that which thou hast ordained for our Nourishment and Preservation, and that thou would'st preserve it to us, that we may have it from day to day, whilst we live in the World with thy Ble<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ssing upon it, that we may not be tempted to take Bread which is not Our's, nor be over solicitous, and careful for to morrow, but by daily Prayer, may obtain daily sup<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />plies from thee, so far as shall be necessary or convenient for us.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debters.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour here doth not teach us the Order, in which we should pray for good things for our selves, only in three Petitions comprehendeth whatsoever we should ask of God. For doubtless, we are obliged acccording to <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 6.32. first to <ns0:hi>seek the Kingdom of God,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>the Righteousness thereof</ns0:hi>: That by our <ns0:hi>Debts</ns0:hi> are here meant our <ns0:hi>Sins,</ns0:hi> is plain from <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 11.4. as also from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 14. of this Chapter, where they are called <ns0:hi>Trespasses</ns0:hi> The Sense is then, discharge us from that Obligat<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>on to De<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>th, which our Sins have laid us under: Give us a Pardon for our sins pa<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t, and present (for who liveth, and sinneth not again<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>t thee?) <ns0:hi>as we forgive our Debters,</ns0:hi> not as <ns0:hi>Perfectly, but in like manner,</ns0:hi> as we according to the im<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />perfect State of our Natures, forgive those who have done us injury, not seeking any Revenge upon them, nor bearing them any Malice, so as indeed those who retaining their Ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lice in their Hearts<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> put up this Prayer unto God, do in Effect pray down Divine Vengeance upon their Souls; well therefore doth the Apostle command 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 2.8. that we should <ns0:hi>lift up pure Hands unto God without Wrath, or doubting.</ns0:hi> So that not only <ns0:hi>Faith,</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>Charity</ns0:hi> also is necessary to our praying acceptably.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 And lead us not into temptation, but de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />liver us from evil, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">1 Chro. 29.11.</ns0:note> For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.<ns0:note place="bottom">The term <ns0:hi>Temptation</ns0:hi> in the General signifieth a <ns0:hi>Tryal,</ns0:hi> and is sometimes used to express <ns0:hi>Go<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>s Tryals</ns0:hi> of his Peoples <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Obedience,</ns0:hi> but most or<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>inarily to express Satans <ns0:hi>Tryals</ns0:hi> of us, by <ns0:hi>Motions to sin,</ns0:hi> which may be from our own Lusts, <ns0:hi>Isa.</ns0:hi> 1. Or, from the Devil, who is therefore called the <ns0:hi>Temp<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ter,</ns0:hi> or from the World. These are the <ns0:hi>Temptations</ns0:hi> which we are Commanded to pray against, not that God leads any Persons into such Temptations, unless <ns0:hi>by the Permission of his Providence.</ns0:hi> But <ns0:hi>deliver us from Evil,</ns0:hi> from the <ns0:hi>Evil one,</ns0:hi> as some read it, because of the Article prefixed, but others think it not <ns0:hi>Material</ns0:hi> whether we under<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tand the <ns0:hi>Devil,</ns0:hi> who is the Evil one, or the <ns0:hi>Evil of Temptations</ns0:hi> which harm us not, if we be not overcome by them. For <ns0:hi>thine is the Kingdom, the Power, and the Glory, for ever</ns0:hi> Amen. These words are omitted by <ns0:hi>Luke, ch.</ns0:hi> 11.4. but many think, that <ns0:hi>Luke</ns0:hi> speaks of another time, when he Dictated this <ns0:hi>Prayer</ns0:hi>: The words both shew us, that the <ns0:hi>Honour and Glory of God</ns0:hi> ought to be the <ns0:hi>End,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Scope</ns0:hi> of all our Prayers, and that we can expect no Audience, but upon the Account of Gods Grace and Mercy, and they likewise confirm our Faith, that God is able to grant, what we ask of him <ns0:hi>Amen</ns0:hi>: This in the cloze of a Sentence is a Particle of <ns0:hi>Wishing,</ns0:hi> and signif<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>eth our Desire to be heard; and as it is a term that signi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fies <ns0:hi>Truth</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Certainty,</ns0:hi> it likewise signifieth our <ns0:hi>Faith</ns0:hi> in God that we shall be heard.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:228" />14 For <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">M<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>r. 11.25. Col. 3.13.</ns0:note> if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="15">15 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 18.35. Jam. 2.13.</ns0:note> if ye forgive not men their trespasses, nei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther will your Father forgive you your trespasses.<ns0:note place="bottom">Not that our meer forgiving our Brethren the Injuries done unto us, is all that God requireth of us in Order to the Forgive<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ness we expect from him, the contrary is plain from seve<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ral other Texts, <ns0:hi>Io.</ns0:hi> 3.18.36. <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 2.38. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 16.31. &c. but that without this Forgiveness of our Brethren, God will not forgive us, <ns0:hi>Mat.</ns0:hi> 18.35. It is one piece of that Obe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dience which we owe to God, and also of our Gratitude without the performance of which it is vain for us to hope for forgiveness from God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 Moreover when ye fast, be not as the hypocrites of a sad countenance, for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 But thou when thou fastest, anoint thine head and wash thy face.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret, and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.<ns0:note place="bottom">Our Saviour in these words returns to his former Work, to caution his Disciples against <ns0:hi>Hypocrisie, Vain Glory,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Ostentation</ns0:hi> in their <ns0:hi>Religious Duties,</ns0:hi> the doing them to be seen of Men, what he before said, as to <ns0:hi>giving Alms,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Prayer</ns0:hi> he here again applyeth, as to <ns0:hi>Private fasting,</ns0:hi> which is by this Discourse of our Saviour confirmed, tho not as a stated, yet as an occasioned Duty of Christians, in Order to<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> and as an Indication of their humbling of their Souls for their sins, or under the mighty hand of God, but he requireth that it should be <ns0:hi>in Sincerity,</ns0:hi> not in <ns0:hi>Hypocrisie,</ns0:hi> for <ns0:hi>the Glory of God,</ns0:hi> not for <ns0:hi>Ostentation</ns0:hi> and appearance unto Men: Our Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />viour probably in this Discourse hath a respect to some Hy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pocritical usages of the <ns0:hi>Pharisees,</ns0:hi> using to Dis-figure their Countenances, and look demurely, or sowrly upon their <ns0:hi>Fasting days,</ns0:hi> not that he prohibiteth here <ns0:hi>Habits,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stures</ns0:hi> suted to the Duty, himself sometimes Commanded the <ns0:hi>Iews to put off their Ornaments,</ns0:hi> nor was any thing more ordinary for good Men then to cover themselves <ns0:hi>with Sackcloth,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>put Ashes on their Heads.</ns0:hi> All that our Lord prohibit<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />eth is the <ns0:hi>Affecting</ns0:hi> of these things, to cover the <ns0:hi>Hypocrisie</ns0:hi> of their Hearts. Nor must we think, that it is the Will of God, that we on such Days, should indeed <ns0:hi>anoint our Heads,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Wash our Faces</ns0:hi>: Or (which is the same thing with us) <ns0:hi>Adorn, Paint,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Perfume</ns0:hi> our <ns0:hi>selves,</ns0:hi> or use any <ns0:hi>Habits,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Gestures</ns0:hi> unsutable to <ns0:hi>Mourning,</ns0:hi> and not <ns0:hi>Indicative</ns0:hi> o<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> afflicted Souls, but that we should rather do this, than the other, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> put on a Mask and Vizard of sorrow for sin, when indeed we had no Sense of it, for still <ns0:hi>we must appea<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap> to our Heavenly Father to fast,</ns0:hi> which we cannot very well do, if our outward Habit and Demeanour, be not something proportioned to the inward Sorrow, and affliction of our Souls, for the putting on of fine Dresses and Ornaments, mu<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> be an imperate Act of the Soul; and not like to be Com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />manded by a Soul in affliction, it being natural to such a Soul to neglect the Culture of the Body, being wholly swal<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed up with bitter Thoughts, relating to its own spiritual and eternal State. Our Saviour addeth the same Argument to press <ns0:hi>sincere Fasting,</ns0:hi> which he had before used concerning the Duty of <ns0:hi>giving Alms</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>secret Prayer,</ns0:hi> where I have before spoken to those Words.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="19">19 Lay <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Prov. 23.4. Heb. 13.5. Jam. 5.20.</ns0:note> not up for your selves treasures on earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where Theeves break thorough and steal.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="20">20 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 12.33.</ns0:note> But lay up for your selves Treasures in heaven, where neither moth, nor rust doth cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rupt, and where theeves do not break through nor steal.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="21">21 For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.<ns0:note place="bottom">A <ns0:hi>Treasure</ns0:hi> (according to the Notation of the Word) signifieth something laid up for to morrow, for <ns0:hi>future time,</ns0:hi> more largely it signifieth any Riches, or what we judge a va<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />luable Portion, make not the things of the Earth, your Ri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ches, or Portion, with reference to <ns0:hi>future time</ns0:hi>; for all the Riches of the Earth are perishing Contemptible things, <ns0:hi>Silver</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Gold</ns0:hi> is what <ns0:hi>R<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>st</ns0:hi> will corrupt, <ns0:hi>Clot<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>es,</ns0:hi> are what <ns0:hi>Moths</ns0:hi> will spoil, any other things are sub<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ect to Casualties; and amongst others, to the violence of unreasonable Men, who tho they have no right to them, will ordinarily take them from you. But let your <ns0:hi>Riches,</ns0:hi> your <ns0:hi>Treasure</ns0:hi> be that which is <ns0:hi>Heavenly,</ns0:hi> those Habits of Grace, which will bring you to Heaven, the things which <ns0:hi>accompany Salvation, Heb.</ns0:hi> 6.9. which <ns0:hi>make you meet to be partakers of the Saints in Light,</ns0:hi> Col. 1.12. be <ns0:hi>Rich in good Works,</ns0:hi> 1 Tim. 6.18. <ns0:hi>lay<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing up in store for your selves, a good Foundation against the time to come, that you may lay hold on Eternal Life, v.</ns0:hi> 19. <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 19.21. <ns0:hi>&</ns0:hi> 25.34. Luk. 18.22. Those Trea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sures will not be liable to such Accidents as all <ns0:hi>Earthly Treasures are</ns0:hi>: Wherever you fix your <ns0:hi>Treasure,</ns0:hi> your Heart will be there also, thinking upon it, delighting in it, &c.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="22">22 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk. 11<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>.</ns0:note> The light of the body is the eye, if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="23">23 But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness; how great <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> that darkness?<ns0:note place="bottom">You had need look to your Hearts, your <ns0:hi>Vnderstanding, Iudgment</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Affections,</ns0:hi> for look what Proportion there is betwixt your <ns0:hi>Bodi<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y Eye,</ns0:hi> and the rest of the Bodily Members, with regard to their Guidance, and Conduct: The same Proportion there is betwixt your <ns0:hi>Heart,</ns0:hi> and whole <ns0:hi>Conver<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sation,</ns0:hi> with reference to the Guidance of it, with relation to God: The Eye is the Window by which the Soul looks out to guide the Body, if that be not impaired by the de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fluction of Humours, &c. but be single, it directs all the Motions of the Body right; but if that be <ns0:hi>Defective,</ns0:hi> or any way impaired, the whole Body is at a loss how to move safely, and with Advantage to it. So if your Hearts be set right, if you have a right and sound Judgment, a true and sanctified Affection, they will influence, and guide all your Actions, your whole Conversation will be regular and Holy: But if that inward <ns0:hi>Eye be Evil,</ns0:hi> through <ns0:hi>Covetousness,</ns0:hi> too much adherence to the Earth, or <ns0:hi>through Envy</ns0:hi> (both which are called <ns0:hi>Evil Eyes</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Scripture</ns0:hi>) or through the <ns0:hi>Preva<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lence</ns0:hi> of any other <ns0:hi>Lusts or Passions,</ns0:hi> your Darkness will be exceeding great: You will not be able to set one step right, for out of the abundance of the Heart the Mouth speaketh, and according to the Dictates and Affections of the Heart, the Hand, and the whole Man acteth.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="24">24 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luk<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 span">
                        <ns0:desc>〈…〉</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                  </ns0:note> No man can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one, and love the other, or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other, you cannot serve God and mammon.<ns0:note place="bottom">No man can serve two Masters, that is two Masters that Command contrary things each to other, for that is the pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />
                     <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ent Case of <ns0:hi>God,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mammon.</ns0:hi> Or, No man with <ns0:hi>the <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>ike Diligence,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Alacrity,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Faithfulness</ns0:hi> can serve <ns0:hi>two Masters.</ns0:hi> It is a proverbial Speech, and in reason to be un<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />derstood of contrary Masters, he will either hate the one, or the first, and love the second, or else he will cleave to the first, and contemn the other, that is, so in his Actions behave himself, that he will appear a true Servant but to one of them, and despise, or <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>ight the other; <ns0:hi>You cannot serve God</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Mammon.</ns0:hi> It is not improbable, that some of the Anci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ents have thought that amongst some of the Heathen, they had an Idol called <ns0:hi>Mammon,</ns0:hi> which they made the God of Money, thence <ns0:hi>Mammon</ns0:hi> by a Figure signifieth <ns0:hi>Riches,</ns0:hi> as <ns0:hi>Luk.</ns0:hi> 16.9. So as it is of an Equivalent <ns0:hi>Sense</ns0:hi> to, no Man can serve God and <ns0:hi>Bacchus,</ns0:hi> or God and <ns0:hi>Venus</ns0:hi>: That is, none can be a Drunkard, or an unclean Person, and a true Servant of God. So no Man can <ns0:hi>serve God,</ns0:hi> and yet make the get<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting of <ns0:hi>Riches</ns0:hi> right or wrong, his Study, hence the Apostle calls <ns0:hi>Covetousness, Idolatry, Col.</ns0:hi> 3.5. So that by <ns0:hi>serving</ns0:hi> here must be understood a giving up of our selves chiefly, or wholly to the Service of God, and to the business of get<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ting the World: Or, serving the latter, in what it Tempteth or Commandeth us to, contrary to the Will of God.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="25">25 Therefore I say, <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Psal. 55<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Luk. 12.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>
                     <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Phil. 4.6 1 Tim. 6 <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">
                        <ns0:desc>••</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> 1. Pet. 5.7.</ns0:note> Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink, nor for your body, what ye shall put on: Is not the life more than meat, or the bo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dy than rayment.<ns0:note place="bottom">The Text must not be interpreted in a Sense Contra<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dictory to those many other Texts, which forbid an idle Life, and Command us, in the sweat of our Face to eat our Bread, or to <ns0:hi>Provide for our Families,</ns0:hi> 2 <ns0:hi>Thess.</ns0:hi> 3.20.11. 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 5.8. nor did Christ himself live such a Life, he <ns0:hi>went about doing good,</ns0:hi> finishing the Work which his Father had given him to do, it must be therefore understood, 1. Of no such thoughts as are inconsistent with the Service of God, mentioned in the last Words. 2. Of no Anxious and Di<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />stracting thoughts. 3. Of no such thoughts as should shew any distrust, and diffidence in Gods providing for us. God hath given us our <ns0:hi>Lives</ns0:hi> and our Bodies, without our care for the Existence of them. Why should we in a law<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ful, and moderate use of means, distrust God for a Sub<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sistence for them, he hath given us the greater, will he not (think you) give us the less?</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="26">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:228" />26 <ns0:note place="margin">Job 38.41. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>sal. 147.9. <ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>uke 12.24.</ns0:note> Behold the fowls of the air, for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns, yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better then they?<ns0:note place="bottom">God takes a care of all his Creatures. For Example, consi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der the <ns0:hi>Fowls,</ns0:hi> and those not the <ns0:hi>Tame Fowls</ns0:hi> about your Hou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ses, but the Fowls of the Air, for whom the House-wifes Hand doth not provide, neither hath God sitted them for any Labour, by which they can procure their Lively-hood, nor doth he require any such thing of them, nor do they labour, yet their <ns0:hi>Creator</ns0:hi> (who is <ns0:hi>your Heavenly Father) feedeth them.</ns0:hi> You have much more reason to trust in God, if you could not Labour, being hindred by his Providence, for you are more excellent beings then sensible Creatures, and you have a further Relation to God, then that of <ns0:hi>Creatures</ns0:hi> to the <ns0:hi>Creator,</ns0:hi> for God is your Heavenly Father, you are in the order of Nature, and especially considering that God is your Father much better than they.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="27">27 Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit to his stature?<ns0:note place="bottom">How Vain a thing is it to distract your selves with Anxi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ous thoughts, about <ns0:hi>your Body,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>your Life</ns0:hi>? all your think<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing will not add a <ns0:hi>Cubit</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>your Stature</ns0:hi>; as your Being, and Existence deriveth from God, so the <ns0:hi>increase of your Stature</ns0:hi> dependeth upon him; likewise he maketh the Child to grow to the <ns0:hi>just Proportion</ns0:hi> which he hath intended him, and beyond that he cannot pass. If Gods Blessing be necessary to this, and so necessary that no thoughts, no means, will add any thing without the <ns0:hi>Divine Blessing,</ns0:hi> what reason have you to take any such thoughts, as you cannot expect he should bless to their desired Effect and Issue?</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="28">28 And why take ye thought for rayment? Consider the lilies of the field how they grow, They toyl not, neither do they spin.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="29">29 And yet I say unto you, that even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="30">30 Wherefore if God so cloth the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, <ns0:hi>shall</ns0:hi> he not much more <ns0:hi>cloth</ns0:hi> you, O ye of little faith?<ns0:note place="bottom">From <ns0:hi>Sensitive</ns0:hi> Creatures, our Lord proceedeth to<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> 
                     <ns0:hi>Vege<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tables,</ns0:hi> an order of Creatures which have more then <ns0:hi>meer being,</ns0:hi> they have also <ns0:hi>Life,</ns0:hi> tho no <ns0:hi>Sense,</ns0:hi> but yet 2 Degrees beneath Man, wanting not only <ns0:hi>Reason</ns0:hi> but <ns0:hi>Sense.</ns0:hi> He shews us from an instance in these, that we have no more reason to be troubled and anxious about <ns0:hi>Clothing,</ns0:hi> then about <ns0:hi>Meat,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Drink. Clothing</ns0:hi> is of no other use, then for <ns0:hi>Warmth</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Ornament,</ns0:hi> for such Clothing as will serve us for <ns0:hi>Warmth,</ns0:hi> a little care will serve the Turn, <ns0:hi>Sudamus ad Supervacanea,</ns0:hi> our Sweating thoughts are mostly for Superfluities in Cloth<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ing, if God see them fit for us, he will also give us them, without so many thoughts about them. Look upon the <ns0:hi>Li<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lies</ns0:hi> (whether he means what we call <ns0:hi>Tulips,</ns0:hi> or other Flow<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ers called <ns0:hi>Lilies,</ns0:hi> which probably those Countries had in great<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />er <ns0:hi>Variety</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Beauty,</ns0:hi> is not worth the arguing) God de<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />signing to glorify himself in those Creatures, tho of meanest orders, hath given them a greater Beauty, then <ns0:hi>Solomon</ns0:hi> had in all his rich Array. To let us know that <ns0:hi>Art</ns0:hi> must not con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tend with <ns0:hi>Nature,</ns0:hi> and that <ns0:hi>Beauty</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Glory</ns0:hi> in <ns0:hi>Apparel</ns0:hi> is no more then is to be found in Creatures much inferiour to our order, which made <ns0:hi>Solon</ns0:hi> (tho an Heathen) prefer the sight of a <ns0:hi>Peacock,</ns0:hi> to that of <ns0:hi>Croesus</ns0:hi>; and therefore this is a thing not worthy of any Anxious thoughts, for if God seeth such things good for us, he that so Clotheth the <ns0:hi>Grass of the Field,</ns0:hi> which is but of a few days Continuance, will much more Cloth us, and if we distrust him for such Provision, we shew our selves Persons of little <ns0:hi>Faith.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="31">31 Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or What shall we drink? or Where<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />withal shall we be clothed?</ns0:p>

                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>tter things This he here pre<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap>et<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> by 2 Ar<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />guments. 1. <ns0:hi>Because these are the things which People spend all their thoughts upon, who are not aware that they have Souls to take care for, or do notunderstand</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>Providence of God,</ns0:hi> or have no such Relation to God, as Christians have who call God Father. 2. You have (saith he) <ns0:hi>an heaven<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                           <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                        </ns0:gap>y Father,</ns0:hi> who being the God of Heaven knoweth what you need, and being your Father will supply also your needs.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="33">33 But <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 12.31. <ns0:hi>See</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Ki.</ns0:hi> 3.13. Psa. 37.</ns0:note> seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness, and all these things shall be added unto you.<ns0:note place="bottom">The <ns0:hi>Kingdom of God, and his Righteousness</ns0:hi> in this Verse are Terms Comprehensive of whatsoever appertaineth to the Honour and Glory of God, either as Means, or as the End, Let your Principal Care, and Study be, how to get to Hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ven, and how to promove the Kingdom of God in the World, to bring your Hearts in Subjection to the Will of God, that the Kingdom of God may be within you, and how to bring others to the Obedience of Faith, and of the Will of God. And for the things of this Life, it shall fare with you as it did with <ns0:hi>Solomon,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 3.12, who asked not Riches and Honour, but had them. You shall have for your necessities, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 37.4, <ns0:hi>Mar.</ns0:hi> 10, 30. 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 4.8.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>

Sufficient unto the day, <ns0:hi>is</ns0:hi> the evil thereof.<ns0:note place="bottom">No such thoughts as before-mentioned, for God will pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vide for you to Morrow, when to Morrow cometh. Besides, every new Day will bring forth some new Cares, you know not what to morrow will bring forth; nor what to Morrow you will have need of, and if you did, why should you tor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ment your selves before the time? it will be time enough when you feel the Evils of a succeeding time, you need not Torment your selves with Prophecying against your selves, what it may be shall never be, or if it be, you had not need Weaken your selves for the encountring such Evils, by a Pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vious Disturbance of your thoughts about them.</ns0:note>
